full_details: You headed a clean sheet and wrote the King's address to his uncle, and the old man's answer, four words. You said the four words several ways. You will play him. Then you went to the yard with the comedy in your hand and the new page left upstairs. Kemp asked what was in the sleeve. The sleeve was empty. By dinner two men had thrown their gages down, and the King stood between them, graceful and wrong. Sixty lines. No blots. On the tables you wrote that he likes to hear himself.
one_sentence: At first light you gave Gaunt his four words, and by dinner the quarrel was sixty lines, the page left at home.
title: Four words, then sixty lines
